contribution: A contract-validated regression harness that wraps ML security tools in typed in-process adapters, runs them against versioned fixtures, and fails pytest on schema drift - with a hard, labeled separation between REAL product adapters and a synthetic smoke-test scaffold.
methods: 1 Load (fixtures) -> 2 Adapt (in-proc) -> 3 Run (tool) -> 4 Validate (schema) -> 5 Assert (contract) -> 6·7 Report (Markdown)
evidence: Cited Python 3.12 CI: 82 passed, 1 skipped; 90.76% statement coverage, same test job.

October 12 real-adapter job 114977020804: genuine scanner integration test passed; CLI logged precision=recall=F1=1.0. Test assertions cover 3 known-bad and 2 known-good configs, with 3 TP, 0 FP, 0 FN.
Historical results/real_hf_scanner.json is absent from the inspected tree. This claim uses the dated CI job, not an invented replacement artifact.
Synthetic run-smoke values are seeded schema plumbing, not measured detector accuracy; no arbitrary smoke-score bar is shown.
limitations: Fixture coverage is finite; gaps possible.
Adapters can go stale if a tool changes internals.
Real adapter gating requires sibling install.
reproduction: Install the documented development dependencies; run python -m pytest tests/ -q. Use the cited job configuration when reproducing coverage.
Benchmark data, adapters and environment requirements are separate; consult poster/13_reproducibility.md and the claim ledger.
